claims.text: Scoping asks about native and web-crawler options first.
claims.excerpt: Is there an existing Native Connector for this Source System, or can it be crawled using the native Glean Web Crawler datasource?

claims.text: Use an existing connector before building a new one.
claims.excerpt: Work to leverage an existing connector first before building a new one

claims.text: Prefer read-only keys.
claims.excerpt: read-only keys are preferred if supported for Content+Permission+Activity data

claims.text: Check source users match SSO users.
claims.excerpt: Do users in the Source System match users in the SSO system associated with Glean?

claims.text: Ask for a sandbox.
claims.excerpt: Is there a Dev/Test/Sandbox environment against which connector development can be tested/validated?

claims.text: Define the viewURL target.
claims.excerpt: Where should users be redirected when they click the document in Glean (viewURL)?

claims.text: Ask whether the API URL is static.
claims.excerpt: Will the API URL stay static?

claims.text: Ask permission change frequency.
claims.excerpt: How often are permissions updated in the Source System?

claims.text: Fallback when no API: export to storage.
claims.excerpt: Can the Source System Export Content to an external data storage location

claims.text: Glean needs content, people, and activity data to build the Knowledge Graph.
claims.excerpt: Activity data Creation, modification, editing, viewing, and sharing timestamps and user information

claims.text: Metadata-only results cannot ground Assistant.
claims.excerpt: Can't be used for GenAI Glean Assistant will not be able to summarize the content

claims.text: Never allow-all 'for now'.
claims.excerpt: Never index sensitive content with an allow-all ACL "for now."

claims.text: Without identity data, a manual user map is needed.
claims.excerpt: Manual map of users to corporate identities needs to be provided

claims.text: No activity means weaker ranking.
claims.excerpt: There would be limited signals available due to no activity being pushed, so rankings of search results will be suboptimal.

claims.text: Custom results can be outranked without signals.
claims.excerpt: Results from your custom connector are more likely to be outranked by results from other connectors due to stronger ranking signals.

claims.text: Index users before referencing them.
claims.excerpt: When using non-anonymous permissions, users need to be indexed before being referenced.

claims.text: Choose hosting before building.
claims.excerpt: Choose where it runs before you build, because it determines how secrets, scheduling, and networking are handled.

claims.text: Run below the source quota.
claims.excerpt: A source allowing 600 requests/minute is 10/second; running at 7-8 leaves room for retries

claims.text: /indexdocument 10 rps; /indexdocuments 600 docs/min.
claims.excerpt: /indexdocument10 requests per second/indexdocuments600 documents per minute

claims.text: Deployment limit: 8,000 rpm across IPs.
claims.excerpt: 8,000 requests per minute across all IP addresses

claims.text: Deployment limit: 100 rps from one IP.
claims.excerpt: 100 requests per second from a single IP address

claims.text: isUserReferencedByEmail decides email vs ID references.
claims.excerpt: This should be set to true if you want to refer to user identities using emails directly.

claims.text: Do not flatten groups into users.
claims.excerpt: Don't flatten groups into user lists

claims.text: No runtime or hosting constraints.
claims.excerpt: Glean places no constraints on where a custom connector runs

claims.text: Scheduling like native connectors applies to Glean-hosted deployments.
claims.excerpt: This is applicable if the connector is deployed in the Glean cloud instance.

claims.text: Self-hosted networking must allow pushes to Glean indexing endpoints.
claims.excerpt: Your environment must allow pushes to Glean's indexing endpoints.

claims.text: Self-host when residency, isolation, or policy requires it.
claims.excerpt: Choose this when data-residency, network isolation, or internal security policies require the connector to run inside your infrastructure.

claims.text: Intersection semantics.
claims.excerpt: A user must belong to every group within one entry; multiple entries are alternative intersections.

claims.text: Common schedule: full nightly or weekly.
claims.excerpt: Full nightly or weekly - reconciles deletions and repairs drift.

claims.text: Full crawls must cover the entire scope.
claims.excerpt: a full crawl must cover the entire confirmed scope before completing, because stale-document deletion removes anything absent from the run.

claims.text: Never let a partial fetch complete as a full crawl.
claims.excerpt: Never let a partial or failed fetch finish as a successful full crawl.

claims.text: Items over 64 MB index metadata and permissions only.
claims.excerpt: If the size is GREATER than 64 MB, the crawler WILL NOT download the item contents and will only download the metadata and permissions information for indexing.

claims.text: Automate token rotation.
claims.excerpt: Automated indexing token rotation

claims.text: Custom connectors ingest data from sources without native support.
claims.excerpt: specialized integrations built to ingest and index data from sources that are not natively supported

claims.text: Indexed mode suits bulk corpora and historical or cross-document questions.
claims.excerpt: Docs, wikis, tickets, knowledge articles, code, and other bulk corpora; historical or cross-document questions.

claims.text: Common schedule: incremental 15–60 min.
claims.excerpt: Incremental every 15-60 minutes - keeps search fresh at low cost.

claims.text: Employee data is separate from ACL identities.
claims.excerpt: It's distinct from the datasource identities (users, groups, memberships) that back document ACLs

claims.text: Rate limiting is proactive; retries are reactive.
claims.excerpt: The rate limiter is proactive

claims.text: Permissions and memberships process asynchronously.
claims.excerpt: Permissions and memberships are processed asynchronously
